seoTitle: Orbital Mechanics Sandbox: N-Body Gravity Simulation with Orbit Trails
metaDescription: Enter bodies with mass, position and velocity and watch their orbits under mutual gravity as trails. Free leapfrog integrator.
intro: Integrates the motion of up to ten bodies under mutual gravity in two dimensions and draws their orbit trails and final state.
why:
Orbits are easy to describe and hard to picture. Enter a Sun, an Earth and a Mars in astronomical units, solar masses and years, and the trails show their ellipses. Change a speed and see how the orbit turns from circle to ellipse to escape.

The integrator is velocity Verlet (leapfrog), which keeps energy and angular momentum from drifting; both drifts are printed. The result was compared with a high-order solver, and it converges as the time step is reduced. Close encounters need a smaller step. The sample masses use the planet to Sun mass ratios from NASA data, and the speeds are circular-orbit values.
howTo: Enter one body per line: name, mass, x, y, vx, vy.
Choose AU/solar mass/year units or arbitrary units with G = 1.
Set the time step and total time.
Read the final state and look at the trails.

faq.q: Why does G equal 4 pi squared?
faq.a: In AU, solar masses and years that makes a circular orbit at 1 AU last one year, an idealisation.

faq.q: How do I know the step is small enough?
faq.a: Halve it and compare the final positions.
There is no collision handling; a very close pass needs a tiny step.
